metaData.title: Spring AI 2.0.0 GA Available Now
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Spring AI 2.0.0 GA is released, featuring a Spring Boot 4 baseline, Jackson 3, null-safety, a refactored options system, a unified tool-calling advisor chain, and official MCP Java SDK integration.
metaData.summary: This article announces the general availability of Spring AI 2.0.0, a major release that re-architects the framework on a Spring Boot 4 and Spring Framework 7 foundation. Key improvements include an upgrade to Jackson 3 for better JSON serialization, full JSpecify null-safety annotations, and a complete refactoring of the options and configuration properties system for consistency and immutability. The core project now focuses on a curated set of chat model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google GenAI, Mistral AI, DeepSeek, Ollama), leveraging vendor SDKs. The most significant architectural change is the lifting of the tool-calling loop into the advisor chain, making it a composable, first-class component via the new `ToolCallingAdvisor`. This enables unified tool calling, progressive tool disclosure for scaling to hundreds of tools, and structured self-correcting output. The release also integrates the official MCP Java SDK 2.0.0, introduces an annotation-driven programming model for MCP servers and clients, and makes Streamable HTTP the default transport. New community extensions for event-sourced conversation memory and agentic patterns are highlighted.

mainPoints.point: Spring AI 2.0 is rebuilt on Spring Boot 4 with a focus on consistency and developer experience.
mainPoints.explanation: The release upgrades to Spring Boot 4.0/4.1 and Spring Framework 7.0, but the deeper value is in the architectural improvements: Jackson 3, full null-safety with JSpecify, and a completely refactored, immutable options system with builders.

mainPoints.point: The tool-calling loop is now a composable advisor in the ChatClient chain.
mainPoints.explanation: Previously buried inside each chat model, the tool loop is now a first-class `ToolCallingAdvisor`. This allows for unified tool calling, progressive tool disclosure (`ToolSearchToolCallingAdvisor`), and structured output self-correction (`StructuredOutputValidationAdvisor`), enabling more sophisticated agentic patterns.

mainPoints.point: MCP integration is a core feature with an annotation-driven programming model.
mainPoints.explanation: Spring AI 2.0 ships with the official MCP Java SDK 2.0.0. The new `mcp-annotations` module allows exposing any Spring service as an MCP server with `@McpTool`, `@McpResource`, and `@McpPrompt`. Streamable HTTP is now the default transport.

mainPoints.point: The core project focuses on a curated set of chat model providers using vendor SDKs.
mainPoints.explanation: To improve quality and adaptability, the core now supports a defined set of providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, etc.) primarily through their official SDKs, with some models maintained directly by vendors like Oracle and Microsoft.

keyQuotes: Spring AI 2.0 lifts the tool loop into the advisor chain as a first-class, composable component.

The improved consistency of Spring AI 2.0 codebase will help, but we also need to provide more guidance to our community in order to make those contributions more useful and integrated in a timely manner.
Streamable HTTP is now the default, replacing the deprecated SSE transport.

relatedArticles.title: Spring AI Agentic Patterns (Part 6): AutoMemoryTools — Persistent Agent Memory Across Sessions
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces AutoMemoryTools for Spring AI, a file-based long-term memory system that enables AI agents to persist curated facts, user preferences, and project decisions across sessions.

relatedArticles.title: Spring AI 1.0.6， 1.1.5， 2.0.0-M5 Available Now
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Spring AI has released versions 1.0.6, 1.1.5, and 2.0.0-M5, with the latter introducing significant breaking changes, new features, and a major SDK migration for OpenAI integration.

relatedArticles.title: Codex Now Integrates Directly with Chrome on macOS and Windows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces a new Chrome extension for Codex on macOS and Windows, enabling the AI to operate directly within a user's live browser session to perform complex, parallel automation tasks using their active profile and direct code execution.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.

relatedArticles.title: Blending Chat with Rich UIs with Spring AI and MCP Apps
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article demonstrates how to build 'MCP Apps' using Spring AI 2.0.0-M3, enabling the integration of rich, interactive HTML UIs directly within AI chat interfaces.

relatedArticles.title: Spring AI Agentic Patterns (Part 7): Session API — Event-Sourced Short-Term Memory with Context Compaction
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the Spring AI Session API, a new event-sourced short-term memory layer for AI agents, featuring turn-safe context compaction, multi-agent branch isolation, and keyword-searchable recall storage.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: Tool Calling in Spring AI 2.0: A Composable， Agentic Architecture
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Spring AI 2.0 rearchitects tool calling as a composable, advisor-chain-based loop, enabling memory integration, progressive tool disclosure, MCP interoperability, and custom extensions.

relatedArticles.title: Andrej Karpathy on Code Agents， AutoResearch， and the Loopy Era of AI
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Andrej Karpathy explores the paradigm shift from manual programming to agent orchestration, the automation of AI research, and the profound implications for software engineering and education.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces GPT-5.5, a new category of AI that acts as an autonomous agent capable of planning, reasoning, and executing complex multi-step tasks across different applications.
